facts.label: official
facts.quote: The total value of ₹2000 banknotes in circulation, which amounted to ₹3.62 lakh crore on March 31, 2023 had declined to ₹3.56 lakh crore as at the close of business on May 19, 2023.
facts.text: The total value of ₹2,000 denomination banknotes in circulation stood at ₹3.56 lakh crore as of May 19, 2023, when the withdrawal from circulation was announced.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Data collected from major banks indicates that out of the total banknotes in ₹2000 denomination received back from circulation, about 87% is in the form of deposits and the remaining around 13% has been exchanged into other denomination banknotes.
facts.text: Approximately 87% of the total ₹2,000 banknotes returned to banks after the withdrawal announcement came in the form of bank deposits rather than over-the-counter exchanges.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Thus, 97.26% of the ₹2000 banknotes in circulation as on May 19, 2023, has since been returned.
facts.text: By November 30, 2023, 97.26% of the ₹2,000 denomination notes circulating on May 19, 2023, had been returned to the banking system.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: With a view to minimise inconvenience to the public, to ensure operational convenience and avoid disruption of the regular activities of bank branches, all banks may exchange ₹2000 banknotes upto a limit of ₹20,000/- at a time.
facts.text: To prevent disruption at bank counters, the central bank allowed members of the public to exchange ₹2,000 notes up to ₹20,000 at a time.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: RBI has conveyed that 89% of ₹2000 denomination notes were issued prior to March 2017 and are close to the end of their useful life which spans from 4-5 years.
facts.text: Roughly 89% of all ₹2,000 notes were issued before March 2017 and were approaching the end of their four-to-five-year expected lifespan.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: With fulfilment of the objective of introduction of ₹2000 denomination and availability of banknotes in other denominations in adequate quantity, printing of ₹2000 banknotes was stopped in 2018-19.
facts.text: Printing of the ₹2,000 denomination note was halted in financial year 2018-19 once currency demand was adequately met by other denominations.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Coin of any denomination not lower than one rupee shall be legal tender for any sum not exceeding one thousand rupee in any single transaction.
facts.text: Under Indian coinage law, coins of ₹1 denomination or higher serve as legal tender for payments up to ₹1,000 in a single transaction.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: For deposits in a banking company or a co-operative bank to which the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of. 1949), applies (including any bank or banking institution referred to in section 51 of that Act) it is obligatory to quote PAN for payment in cash for an amount exceeding fifty thousand rupees during any one day (refer Rule 114B).
facts.text: Under Income Tax Rule 114B, quoting a PAN is compulsory for cash deposits exceeding ₹50,000 in a bank during any single day.
